title: Mumbai D2C skincare brand cut Meta dependence 82% → 54% after a CAC shock, recovering blended CAC ₹910 → ₹640
content: SITUATION: A Mumbai D2C skincare brand at ₹38L/month revenue (tier-1/2 buyers) ran 82% of its ₹11L monthly ad budget on Meta. In March, iOS signal loss plus festive auction heat pushed blended Meta CAC from ₹540 to ₹910 in five weeks and dropped Meta ROAS 3.1x → 1.9x. One platform now controlled the entire P&L. ACTION: We capped Meta at 55% of budget and redeployed the rest. On Google we put ₹2.4L into Performance Max plus branded and category Search ('vitamin C serum for oily skin'), landing CAC at ₹620 on high-intent traffic. We built WhatsApp flows for abandoned carts and COD confirmation, recovering 14% of dropped orders at near-zero CAC. We listed hero SKUs on Amazon.in to capture the demand our own ads were creating, and pushed founder-led Instagram Reels plus YouTube how-to content for organic pull. OUTCOME: Over 11 weeks Meta fell to 54% of spend, blended CAC settled at ₹640 (down 30% from the ₹910 peak), and blended ROAS recovered to 2.8x. Organic plus WhatsApp now drive 19% of revenue, so the next auction spike no longer threatens survival.
lesson: Track a 'single-channel exposure' number the way you track ROAS. Past ~70% of spend on one auction-priced platform, you have outsourced your CAC to a market you cannot control, and the shock always lands during peak season when you can least afford it. Diversify before the spike, not during it — and weight the shift toward owned channels (WhatsApp, organic, Amazon.in demand capture) that structurally lower blended CAC, not just paid channels that move the dependence sideways from Meta to Google.
